VII.}}</noinclude>vvith an other man. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=4}}† Therfore my brethren {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Being now baptised and dead to sinne, & engraffed in Christs mystical body, you are discharged of the Lavv of Moyses, and are free in Christ.}}∷ you also are made dead to the Lavv by the body of Christ: that you may be an other mans vvho is risen againe from the dead, that vve may fructifie to God. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=5}}† For vvhen vve vvere in the flesh, the passions of sinnes, that vvere by the Lavv, did vvorke in our members, to fructifie vnto death. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=6}}† but novv vve are loosed from the lavv of death, vvherein vve vvere deteined: c {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''ὥστε δουλεύειν''}}∷ in so much we serue in {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ By Baptisme we haue not Christes iustice imputed to vs, but an inward newnesse of spirit giuen vs and resident in vs.}}∷ nevvnesse of spirit, and not in the oldnes of the letter.

{{verse|chapter=7|verse=7}}† VVhat shal we say then? is the Lavv sinne? God forbid. But sinne I did not knovv, but by the Lavv. for concupiscence I knevv not, vnlesse the lavv did say: {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Exo. 20, 17. Deu. 5, 21.''}}* ''{{sup|‖}} Thou shalt not couet''. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=8}}† But {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Sinne or concupiscence which was a sleepe before, vvas wakened by prohibition, the Law not being the cause thereof, nor giuing occasion thereunto, but occasion being taken by our corrupt nature to resist that vvhich was commaunded.}}∷ occasion being taken, sinne by the commaundement vvrought in me al concupiscence. For vvithout the Lavv sinne vvas dead. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=9}}† And I liued vvithout the Lavv sometime. But vvhen the commaundement vvas come, sinne reuiued. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=10}}† And I vvas dead: and the commaundement, that vvas vnto life, the same to me vvas found to be vnto death. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=11}}† For sinne taking occasion by the commaundement, seduced me, and by it killed me. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=12}}† Therfore {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''1. Tim. 1, 8.''}}* the Lavv in deede is holy, and the commaundement holy, and iust, and good.

{{verse|chapter=7|verse=13}}† That then vvhich is good, to me vvas it made death? God forbid. but sinne, that it may appeare sinne, by the good thing vvrought me death: that sinne might become sinning aboue measure by the commaundement. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=14}}† For vve knovv that the Law is spiritual, but I am carnal, sold vnder sinne. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=15}}† For {{sup|‖}} that which I vvorke, I vnderstand not. for {{sup|‖}} not that vvhich I vvil, the same do I: but vvhich I hate, that I doe. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=16}}† And if that vvhich I vvil not, the same I do: I consent to the Lavv, that it is good.

{{verse|chapter=7|verse=17}}† But novv, not I vvorke it any more, but the sinne that dvvelleth in me. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=18}}† For I know that there dvvelleth not in me, that is to say, in my flesh, good. For to vvil, is present vvith me, but to accomplish that vvhich is good, I finde not. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=19}}† For {{sup|‖}} not the good vvhich I vvil, that do I: but the euil {{sup|‖}} vvhich I vvil not, that I do. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=20}}† And if that vvhich I vvil not, the same I doe: novv not I vvorke it, but the sinne that dvvelleth in me. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=21}}† I finde therfore, the Lavv, to me hauing a vvil to doe good, that euil is present vvith me. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=22}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ The Epistle in a Votiue Masse for sinnes.}}∷ For I am delighted vvith the lavv of God according to the invvard man: {{verse|chapter=7|verse=23}}† but I see an other lavv in my members, repugning to the lavv of my minde, and captiuing me in the lavv of sinne, that<noinclude>{{rh|||is}}</noinclude>
